items.title: ISC BIND 9: the DNSSEC validator checks every RRSIG in a response with no short-circuit once one valid signature confirms the RRset, so a zone with many signatures can exhaust resolver CPU (denial of service).
items.mapping: Resource exhaustion or a crash: this breaks availability, not the integrity of answers.

items.title: PowerDNS Recursor (ZoneToCache): records that fall outside the loaded zone's bailiwick are inserted into the shared cache, letting a malicious or compromised authoritative server poison cached answers for arbitrary names.
items.mapping: The resolver cached records it was never asked for or that lie outside the server's zone — the Kaminsky payload (Part III).

items.title: Netty netty-resolver-dns: buildAliasMap caches CNAME records without checking the responding server is authoritative for them (missing bailiwick check), allowing an on-path attacker to inject a CNAME that redirects later lookups.
items.mapping: The resolver cached records it was never asked for or that lie outside the server's zone — the Kaminsky payload (Part III).

items.title: NLnet Labs Unbound: promiscuous RRsets placed in the authority section (e.g. MX with A/AAAA in additional) can be treated as in-zone delegation data and cached, redirecting clients until the poisoned entries expire.
items.mapping: The resolver cached records it was never asked for or that lie outside the server's zone — the Kaminsky payload (Part III).

items.title: dnsmasq: a heap buffer overflow in extract_name() can inject false DNS cache entries that redirect queries to attacker-controlled IPs, or crash the service.
items.mapping: A memory-safety bug while parsing DNS messages — the deck's warning that 'parsing names correctly is central'.

items.title: ISC BIND 9: a weakness in the pseudo-random number generator lets an attacker predict source ports and query IDs, making it feasible to inject forged responses into resolver caches.
items.mapping: Reply-matching values (transaction ID / source port) were predictable, so an off-path attacker can win the race (Part II).

items.title: ISC BIND 9: recursive resolvers accept certain unsolicited resource records in responses and cache them, violating bailiwick principles and enabling cache poisoning.
items.mapping: The resolver cached records it was never asked for or that lie outside the server's zone — the Kaminsky payload (Part III).

items.title: NLnet Labs Unbound: unsolicited NS records in the authority section were treated as in-zone delegation data and overwrote cached delegation, allowing domain hijacking via spoofed or fragmented replies (non-DNSSEC data).
